Subject: Immediate: Tenant routing fallback execution for targeted regional peering disruption

Megan / Acme ops team —

Short update and action guidance: we’ve observed a targeted peering disruption impacting a subset of US, EU, and APAC egress paths that is increasing tail latency for some tenant traffic and causing intermittent connection timeouts for short windows. Our engineering team has activated the automated fallback but we recommend an opt-in tenant-level execution that will reduce your risk of request failures while we stabilize upstream peering.

What this means for you now
- Most requests should continue to complete; some requests routed through the affected peering may see increased latency (200–800ms variability) or occasional timeouts for <2% of calls.
- If you run latency-sensitive inference (interactive agents, UI-driven calls), we recommend switching traffic to our regional endpoints or enabling the tenant routing override below.

Immediate ask (takes ~5–10 minutes):
1) Confirm you can apply the short DNS TTL change below or accept the header override (we can patch via API) — reply to this thread with the preferred option.
2) If you expect elevated load this morning, let us know; we can provision temporary burst capacity on Dedicated pools for the window.

Recommended short-term options (pick one):
A) API header override (quickest) — set X-Redwood-Region-Hint header to your preferred region (us | eu | apac). Example: X-Redwood-Region-Hint: us
B) Switch to regional endpoint (recommended if you control client config) — us.api.redwood.ai, eu.api.redwood.ai, apac.api.redwood.ai.
C) DNS TTL short path (if you rely on a single hostname) — reduce your app-level DNS cache TTL to 30s to allow faster reroute.

We’ve attached a short runbook (routing-priority_runbook.pdf) and a temporary-proxy-config.snippet for teams that want to add a proxy-based header injection. I’m also copying Ben and Laura who will track provisioning and validation.

Please reply with your choice and we’ll execute immediately.

—

Megan — great questions, quick answers and exact steps below.

Answers
1) Authentication: regional endpoints and header overrides use the same API key surface. No key rotation required. Keys are validated by tenant id + signature; switching endpoints preserves auth.
2) Fallback behavior: region_hint is a soft preference. If we detect capacity constraints in the preferred region, the request may transparently route to the next available region. We will add an explicit "must-route" option if you need hard pinning (not recommended during an ongoing peering recovery).
3) KV cache / session: KV cache is a per-model per-tenant cache on the serving side. If you move requests between regions you may see some cold-start cache misses for existing sessions until the cache warms in the new region. For short interactive flows this is usually a one or two extra-token cost.

Execution steps (header override — fastest, recommended if you can push a header from your proxy)
- Add header: X-Redwood-Region-Hint: us
- Optional: X-Redwood-Fallback-Mode: permissive (default) or strict (no cross-region)

Example curl (header injection):
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer ${REDWOOD_API_KEY}" -H "X-Redwood-Region-Hint: us" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-instruct-3b","input":"Hello"}'

Example Node snippet (axios):
const axios = require('axios');
await axios.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', { input: 'Hi' }, {
  headers: {
    'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}`,
    'X-Redwood-Region-Hint': 'us'
  }
});

If you prefer regional hostnames (longer-term for this window):
- us.api.redwood.ai (preferred for US clients)
- eu.api.redwood.ai
- apac.api.redwood.ai

Notes on monitoring and validation
- We’ll enable a temporary alert that fires on request error rate > 0.5% for your tenant; Ben will confirm the alert id in separate message.
- Please run a smoke test hitting a low-traffic path and share response times (curl + timing) so we can validate on our side.

Attachments: temporary-proxy-config.snippet (example Envoy patch), routing-priority_runbook.pdf (short checklist)

If you give us a quick "go header" now we’ll make the change on our opt-in routing and validate end-to-end.

—
Kimberly
